prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1471; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured's vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the collision happened as described, and scene photos are consistent with the other driver's account. The claimant is confirmed as an occupant of the vehicle at the time of impact. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck pain consistent with whiplash. The injury fits well with the kind and force of this impact. Vehicle records show no prior damage, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy coverage start.

Entry 4: Medical records show the claimant had a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully. Treatment since this collision followed a usual course and tapered as the patient improved. It is not yet clear whether all of the claimed damage stems from this impact, so the medical review is ongoing.

Entry 5: Claimant has added some small details to the account since the first statement, but the core description of the accident has not changed. Counsel has been asked to provide the complete treatment history.

Entry 6: File is pending the medical review and the attorney's response to the request for records. Reserve kept at current level until the causation question is resolved.
